case_name: Sudhir Sharma Son Of Mr. Bajrang Lal ... vs The Chief Secretary

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sudhir Sharma Son Of Mr. Bajrang Lal Sharma, Aged About 36 Years
parties.respondent_defendant: The Chief Secretary, The State Government Of Rajasthan and others

facts_of_case: Estranged husband preferred writ petition against ex-wife-respondent No.4 levelling allegations that she was not eligible for appointment and prayed to carry out a swift inquiring of the testimonials of all the candidates who got employment and recover the amount paid in the form of salary to respondent No.4.

legal_principles.principle: A person may apply under the divorced quota even though an appeal is pending before the High Court.
legal_principles.held: As on today, status of the respondent would be treated as a divorcee. While it is true that under Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a person may not be allowed to re-marry during pendency of the appeal, however the same would not be an essential requirement for applying under the divorced quota.

legal_principles.principle: Dowry given even on demand by the parents of the respondent does not constitute an offence.
legal_principles.held: The present respondent No.4 cannot be held to have committed the offence and the same would not constitute as sufficient to deny her appointment.

legal_principles.principle: Information sought under the Right to Information Act may be denied if it is of personal nature relating to any other individual.
legal_principles.held: The disclosure would be barred in view of the provisions of Section 8 of the Act, which is reproduced as under: 'Exemption from disclosure of information.-- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, there shall be no obligation to give any citizen,--'

outcome.final_order: Appointment under divorcee quota was illegal; petitioner prayed for swift inquiring of testimonials and recovery of amount paid in the form of salary to respondent No.4.
